```{r}
#| label: Libraries setup
#| results: hide

#Load Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
```

My overstory data was taken at the same time that understory data was collected. The methodology for collecting this data follows the same principle as point-intercept understory data. Any vegetation 2m or below intercepting the pole was classified as understory, while vegetation greater than 2m for canopy species (MetPol, AcaKoa, SopChr, and MyrFay) was classified as overstory. Any point without overstory was marked as NoCan (no canopy).

The same function that read the understory data and compiled it into a wide tally can also be used to translate the raw overstory data.

```{r}
#| label: Overstory percentage by Augment Type
#| results: hide
#| fig-size: "150%"

#Species Matrix function
Species_Matrix <-function(data,
                          output = here("Data","WideData","UnderstoryCover_Tally.csv"),
                          plot_col = "Plot_ID",
                          taxon_col = "Taxon_Code"){
  #columns as symbols
  plot_col <- ensym(plot_col)
  taxon_col <- ensym(taxon_col)
  
  #summary generation
  summary_matrix <- data|>
    #filter any missing records
    filter(!is.na(!!taxon_col))|>
    #group by plot and taxon code, then tally
    group_by(!!plot_col,!!taxon_col)|>
    summarise(tally = n(),.groups = "drop")|>
    #pivot data wide
    pivot_wider(names_from = !!taxon_col,
                values_from = tally)
  
  #export dataframe as csv
  write_csv(summary_matrix, output)
  
  message("Species tally matrix successfully saved to: ", output)
  return(summary_matrix)
}


#read in raw overstory data
OverstoryData_Raw <- read.csv(here("Data","RawData","OverstoryData_Raw.csv"))
head(OverstoryData_Raw)


#create grouping labels for overstory raw data
Overstory_Data_byCoverType <- OverstoryData_Raw %>%
  group_by(Plot_ID, Point_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    temp_cat = case_when(
      Veg_Type_Repeats %in% "Native_Can" ~ "Native Canopy",
      Veg_Type_Repeats %in% "Invasive_Can" ~ "Exotic",
      Veg_Type_Repeats == "No_Canopy" ~ "No Canopy",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Check for duplicates of the exact veg type
    New_Status = if_else(
      !is.na(temp_cat) & !duplicated(Veg_Type_Repeats), 
      temp_cat, 
      NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-temp_cat) %>%
  ungroup()

#convert raw data to tally using Species_Matrix function
Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType <- Species_Matrix(Overstory_Data_byCoverType,taxon_col = "New_Status",output = here("Data","WideData","OverstoryPlot_Tally_byCoverType.csv"))
head(Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType)

#convert tally to percentages
Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType <- Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType|>
  #divide by total plot points then multiply by 100 for percentage
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ (.x / 93) * 100))
write_csv(Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType,file = here("Data","WideData","OverstoryPlot_Tally_byCoverType.csv"))
  
#pivot long for graphing, replace NA with 0
Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Long <- Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType|>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `Native Canopy`:Exotic,
    names_to = "Canopy_Type",
    values_to = "Percentages")|>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(., 0)))|>
#add grouping columns
mutate(
  # Extract the number from Plot_ID for BBB/BBN plots
  plot_num = parse_number(Plot_ID),
  # Assign Times_Burned based on prefix and number
  Times_Burned = case_when(
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "UB") ~ 0,
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB|BBN") & plot_num %in% 1:10 ~ 1,
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB|BBN") & plot_num %in% 11:20 ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ),
  Augment = case_when(
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "UB") ~ "Control",
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB") ~ "No",
    str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBN") ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
) |>
  select(-plot_num)
head(Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Long)

#ggplot boxplot
ggplot(Overstory_Plot_Tally_byCoverType_Long,
       aes(x = Augment,
           y = Percentages)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 16) +
  facet_wrap(~ Canopy_Type) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10))+
  labs(
    title = "Canopy Plot Percentage by Augment Type",
    subtitle = "Shown in Plot Percent Cover",
    x = "Augmentation",
    y = "Percentage Cover in Plot"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

On the whole, canopy is sparse for nearly all sites. Perhaps a better way to visualize the data would be to compare the percentages of the three most common canopy species (MetPol, AcaKoa, MyrFay) across the different Augmentation classes.

```{r}
#| label: Overstory species percentages by augmentation status
#| results: hide
#| fig-size: "150%"

Overstory_Plot_Tally <- Species_Matrix(OverstoryData_Raw,output = here("Data","WideData","OverstoryPlot_Tally.csv"))

#pivot data long, add grouping variables
Overstory_Plot_Tally_Long <- Overstory_Plot_Tally|>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ (.x / 93) * 100))|>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = MetPolCan:SopChrCan,
    names_to = "Canopy_Species",
    values_to = "Percentages")|>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(., 0)))|>
  mutate(
    # Extract the number from Plot_ID for BBB/BBN plots
    plot_num = parse_number(Plot_ID),
    # Assign Times_Burned based on prefix and number
    Times_Burned = case_when(
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "UB") ~ 0,
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB|BBN") & plot_num %in% 1:10 ~ 1,
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB|BBN") & plot_num %in% 11:20 ~ 2,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    Augment = case_when(
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "UB") ~ "Control",
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBB") ~ "No",
      str_starts(Plot_ID, "BBN") ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )|>
  select(-plot_num)|>
  #remove NoCan and SopChrCan to only show three main canopy species
  filter(!Canopy_Species %in% c("NoCan", "SopChrCan"))

#visualize as ggplot
ggplot(Overstory_Plot_Tally_Long,
       aes(x = Augment,
           y = Percentages)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 16) +
  facet_wrap(~ Canopy_Species,scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Canopy Species Percentage by Augment Type",
    subtitle = "Shown in Plot Percent Cover",
    x = "Taxon Code",
    y = "Percentage Cover in Plot"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

I also developed a function called Shady, which evaluates all unique plot points which contain overstory. The function identifies whether a given plot point has overstory presence, then creates a list of all the understory species found below. This allows me to analyze the composition of shaded understory vs. exposed understory. One of my hypotheses was that native cover proportion would be higher under canopy, where light levels and leaf litter may suppress the growth of invasive grasses.

```{r}
#| label: Shady function
#| results: hide

Shady <- function(understory_data,
                  overstory_data,
                  overstory_column = Taxon_Code,
                  exclude = "NoCan",
                  include = NULL,
                  file_path = NULL) {
  
  if (!is.null(include)) {
    overstory_points <- overstory_data |>
      filter({{ overstory_column }} %in% include) |>
      select(Plot_ID, Point_ID) |>
      distinct()
  } else {
    overstory_points <- overstory_data |>
      filter(!({{ overstory_column }} %in% exclude)) |>
      select(Plot_ID, Point_ID) |>
      distinct()
  }
  
  understory_points <- understory_data |>
    inner_join(overstory_points, by = c("Plot_ID", "Point_ID"))
  
  if (!is.null(file_path)) {
    write_csv(understory_points, file_path)
  }
  
  return(understory_points)
}


#dividing all canopy types
Understory_Below_Canopy_all <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,file_path=here("Data","RawData","Understory_Below_Canopy_all.csv"))

Understory_No_Canopy_all <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,include = "NoCan",file_path = here("Data","RawData","Understory_No_Canopy_all.csv"))

Understory_Native_Canopy_all <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,exclude = c("NoCan","MyrFayCan"),file_path = here("Data","RawData","Understory_No_Canopy_all.csv"))

Understory_Below_MetPol <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,include = "MetPolCan",file_path = here("Data","RawData","Understory_Below_MetPol.csv"))

Understory_Below_AcaKoa <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,include = "AcaKoaCan",file_path = here("Data","RawData","Understory_Below_AcaKoa.csv"))

Understory_Below_MyrFay <- Shady(UnderstoryData_Raw,OverstoryData_Raw,include = "MyrFayCan",file_path = here("Data","RawData","Understory_Below_MyrFay.csv"))

#visualizing most common species under different canopy types

#all canopy
Understory_Below_Canopy_all |>
  count(Taxon_Code, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  { \(df)
    ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Taxon_Code, -n), y = n)) +
      geom_col() +
      labs(
        title = "Top 10 Most Frequent Understory Taxa-All Canopy",
        subtitle = paste("n =", nrow(Understory_Below_Canopy_all)),
        x = "Taxon Code",
        y = "Count"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  }()

#no canopy
Understory_No_Canopy_all |>

        title = "Top 10 Most Frequent Understory Taxa-No Canopy",
        subtitle = paste("n =", nrow(Understory_No_Canopy_all)),
        x = "Taxon Code",
        y = "Count"
      ) +

  }()

#under native canopy
Understory_Native_Canopy_all |>

#under ohia canopy
Understory_Below_MetPol |>

    ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Taxon_Code, -n), y = n)) +

Understory_Below_AcaKoa |>
```
